question: If X is the number of 6s obtained in 10 throws of a die, then the variance of X is:
solution:
The correct answer is** 25/18.**

__

• Using the formula, Var(X)=10×16×(1−16)=10×16×56=5036=2518" id="MathJax-Element-815-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">Var(X)=10×16×(1−16)=10×16×56=5036=2518Var(X)=10×16×(1−16)=10×16×56=5036=2518" id="MathJax-Element-642-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">Var(X)=10×16×(1−16)=10×16×56=5036=2518Var(X)=10×16×(1−16)=10×16×56=5036=2518
 Var(X)=10×16×(1−16)=10×16×56=5036=2518
 \text{Var}(X) = 10 \times \frac{1}{6} \times \left(1 - \frac{1}{6}\right) = 10 \times \frac{1}{6} \times \frac{5}{6} = \frac{50}{36} = \frac{25}{18} . Hence, the correct answer is 25/18.
 
• **Incorrect Option (2):** This option provides a date, which is irrelevant to the problem.
 
• **Incorrect Option (3):** Similar to option 2, this option also provides a date, which is incorrect.
 
• Incorrect Option (4): The value 25/9 is incorrect as it does not follow from the binomial variance formula.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 The variance of the number of 6s in 10 throws of a die is a classic example of a binomial distribution problem. Here, the number of trials (n) is 10, and the probability of success (p) in each trial is 1/6.
